title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance, and Manager Guide (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and templates for: hiring, onboarding, the performance and feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers. Follow the checklists and templates below to ensure consistency, legal compliance, and a high-quality candidate and employee experience.

Table of contents
1) Hiring process overview
2) Interview loop and scorecards
3) Offer and negotiation checklist
4) New-hire onboarding (0–90 days)
5) Manager responsibilities and 1:1s
6) Performance review and calibration process
7) Feedback best practices and corrective action
8) Templates and links

---

1) Hiring process overview

Purpose: Reduce time-to-hire while maintaining candidate quality, reduce bias, and ensure clear ownership at each stage.

Stages (owner in parentheses):
- Requisition approval (Hiring manager + Finance) — open headcount validation, level, and compensation band.
- Sourcing (Recruiter) — passive outreach, job boards, internal referrals.
- Screen (Recruiter / Hiring manager) — 30-min phone screen to qualify basic skills and alignment.
- Technical/functional loop (Interview panel) — role-specific assessments and scorecards.
- Final interview + hiring manager calibration (Hiring manager + interviewers) — holistics + risk review.
- Offer (Recruiter + Hiring manager) — compensation, start date, and terms.
- Background & paperwork (Recruiter / People Ops) — reference checks, I-9/contract, equity paperwork where applicable.

SLOs and targets:
- Time to first screen: within 5 business days of requisition approval.
- Time to offer (from first onsite/loop): median 14 calendar days.
- Minimum interview panel size: 3 for IC roles, 4 for manager roles.

Ownership and approvals:
- Hiring manager: role profile, interviewers, final hiring decision (with input from panel).
- Recruiter: candidate pipeline, scheduling, offer coordination.
- People Ops: compensation band approval, background checks, relocation and visa support.

Diversity & inclusion guardrails:
- Use diverse interview panels when possible.
- A minimum of one structured behavioral question and one technical assessment per loop.
- Avoid requirements that are not strictly job-critical (list these in the job profile).

---

2) Interview loop and scorecards

Principles:
- Structure reduces bias: each interviewer asks pre-defined questions and completes a scorecard.
- Focus on role outcomes and measurable signals.

Scorecard template (use the standard Google Form linked in Templates):
- Competency areas (numerical 1–5 and free-text):
  1) Role-specific skills (e.g., system design, model serving)
  2) Problem solving / cognitive ability
  3) Collaboration & communication
  4) Impact & ownership
  5) Culture add / alignment with Redwood values
- Recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / No hire / Defer + short rationale (2–3 sentences)

Interview loop example (Backend ML Engineering role):
1) Recruiter screen (30m) — core expectations, relocation, salary band, visa.
2) Technical coding (60m) — paired coding or take-home; evaluate correctness and clarity.
3) System & infra design (60m) — model-serving or infra design with whiteboard.
4) Cross-functional + collaboration (45m) — product/design partner perspective.
5) Manager interview (45m) — growth, career trajectory, and fit.
6) Hiring committee calibration (30m) — review scorecards and hiring risks.

De-duplication & conflict-of-interest:
- Interviewers must recuse themselves if they have a close personal relationship with the candidate.
- If a candidate previously interviewed with Redwood within 12 months, note prior feedback in the new loop.

---

3) Offer and negotiation checklist

Pre-offer checklist (Recruiter + Hiring manager):
1) Confirm final compensation band and sign-off from Finance.
2) Confirm role level and title.
3) Confirm start date range and relocation/remote details.
4) Confirm equity grant range and refresh policy applicable.
5) Confirm required approvals for signatory.

Offer email should include (template in Templates):
- Base salary, bonus if any, equity grant, target start date, manager name, primary work location, and benefits summary.
- Contingencies (background check, right-to-work).

Negotiation guidance for managers:
- Use bands and justification: quality of competing offers, candidate seniority, and internal equity.
- Escalate exceptions to People Ops for approval.

---

4) New-hire onboarding (0–90 days)

Goals: Ensure new hires are productive, integrated, and understand goals and culture. Managers are accountable for onboarding execution.

Pre-boarding (Recruiter / People Ops) — before Day 1:
- Complete paperwork, benefits enrollment links, and equipment survey.
- Provision accounts (Slack, GitHub, internal wiki, email) and order equipment.
- Send Day 1 agenda and 30/60/90 expectations.

Day 1–7 (Manager checklist):
- Welcome meeting and team lunch (virtual or in-person).
- Set up technical environment: dev machine, VPN, repo access.
- Assign first small project + buddy (peer mentor).
- 1:1 with manager: clarify immediate goals and success signals.

30-day outcomes (Manager / New hire):
- Completed onboarding checklist items.
- Delivered first small project or contribution.
- Shared learning plan and initial career goals.

60-day outcomes:
- Independent contribution on core team tasks.
- Midpoint feedback meeting documented in HRIS.

90-day outcomes and hire confirmation:
- Manager confirms role fit against expectations.
- If performance concerns, open an early performance plan (see section 7).

Suggested onboarding timeline (table):
| Period | Owner | Focus | Deliverables |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-boarding | Recruiter/People Ops | Paperwork, access | Signed docs, accounts provisioned |
| Day 1 | Manager | Orientation | Team intro, initial task |
| Week 1 | Buddy/Manager | Environment + docs | Repo access, runbook read |
| 30 days | Manager | First deliverable | PR merged, demo |
| 60 days | Manager | Autonomy checkpoints | Independent task ownership |
| 90 days | Manager/People Ops | Confirmation | OKR alignment, role confirmation |

---

5) Manager responsibilities and 1:1s

Manager responsibilities (high-level):
- Set clear expectations and measurable goals.
- Run regular 1:1s and provide ongoing feedback.
- Complete career and performance discussions and advocate for team members in calibration.
- Ensure psychological safety and manage workload.

1:1 cadence and structure:
- Frequency: weekly for ICs, weekly or biweekly for managers depending on scope.
- Suggested agenda:
  1) Quick personal check-in (2–3m)
  2) Progress on goals / blockers (10–15m)
  3) Career development & growth (10m)
  4) Action items and follow-ups (2–3m)

Meeting norms:
- Document notes and action items in the team's shared doc.
- 1:1 is private and should avoid surprises at review time.

Promotion and leveling guidance:
- Use the public leveling rubric stored in Product > Requirements.
- Manager provides concrete examples for promotion packets (impact, scope, leadership).

---

6) Performance review and calibration process

Cadence:
- Formal performance reviews occur twice per year (mid-year and year-end) with lightweight quarterly check-ins.

Review timeline (high level):
- 6 weeks before: People Ops opens review cycle and shares timeline.
- 4 weeks before: Self-assessments due.
- 3 weeks before: Peer & cross-functional feedback collected.
- 1 week before: Manager summary and calibration packet due.
- Review week: Calibration and final ratings issued; compensation recommendations submitted.

Components of a review:
- Self-assessment (contributions, challenges, goals)
- Manager assessment (impact, competencies, growth areas)
- Peer feedback (structured prompts)
- Calibration packet (evidence & examples)

Rating scale and guidance:
- Use a four-band system: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Partially Meets / Below Expectations.
- Managers must provide 2–3 concrete evidence points for each rating and a development plan for below expectations.

Calibration principles:
- Calibration committees include cross-functional managers and HR partners.
- Focus on evidence and outcomes rather than intent.
- Address potential rating inflation and ensure internal equity.

Compensation cycles:
- Compensation recommendations accompany year-end reviews.
- People Ops reviews market data and makes final approvals.

---

7) Feedback best practices and corrective action

Continuous feedback:
- Normalize frequent, small-cycle feedback: real-time praise and course-correcting feedback.
- Encourage written feedback for tracking.

Constructive feedback framework (SBI):
- Situation: Describe when and where.
- Behavior: Describe observable behavior.
- Impact: Describe the effect on team/project.
- Suggestion: Offer a concrete next step.

Addressing performance issues:
- Informal coaching: manager documents feedback and timeline; typical duration 2–6 weeks.
- Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): 30–90 days depending on severity.
  - PIP must include clear goals, success measures, resources, and check-in cadence.
  - People Ops must be engaged prior to issuing a PIP and review legal implications for role.
- Escalation: If the PIP is unsuccessful, follow HR/Legal guidance for separation.

Confidentiality & documentation:
- Document all feedback conversations in HRIS or secure manager notes.
- Share documentation only with People Ops and Legal on a need-to-know basis.

---

8) Templates and links

Included templates (linked in central Templates page):

Related pages and resources:

- Global benefits summary (by country)

Appendix: Quick checklists

Hiring manager quick checklist:
1) Complete role profile & banding with People Ops.
2) Confirm interview panel and scorecards.
3) Attend calibration and provide evidence.

Manager first-week checklist for new hires:
1) Set up 1:1 schedule.
2) Assign buddy and first project.
3) Share 30/60/90 expectations.

Performance check-in triggers (manager should act if any of the following occur):
- Missed deadlines without communication for 2+ sprints.
- Repeated quality regressions on PRs or model rollouts.
- Feedback from multiple peers indicating collaboration issues.

---

Ownership and escalation
- People Ops is the single source of truth for policy and templates.
- Hiring disputes (offers, counter-offers, band exceptions) escalate to People Ops -> Finance -> CEO for final approval if needed.
- Performance and disciplinary processes escalate People Ops -> Legal for review.

---

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel). Review cadence: annually or after major policy/legal changes.
- Change log: major updates must include reviewer names and a one-line summary.

End of document
